facts.statement: Guidraco was described and named by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander W.A. Kellner, Jiang Shunxing, and Cheng Xin in 2012 based on the holotype specimen IVPP V17083.
facts.quote: Guidraco is known only from the holotype specimen IVPP V17083, described and named by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander W.A. Kellner, Jiang Shunxing and Cheng Xin in 2012.

facts.statement: The Guidraco holotype was collected from the Jiufotang Formation near Sihedang, Liaoning Province, dating to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected at Sihedang near Lingyuan City in the Liaoning Province from the Jiufotang Formation, dating to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, about 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Guidraco measures 38 cm in length.
facts.quote: The holotype skull of Guidraco has a length of 38 cm.

facts.statement: Guidraco has distinctive teeth, including a long, narrow first upper tooth and three subsequent enormous, robust, pointed, and slightly recurved teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth of Guidraco are very distinctive. Of the twenty-three teeth of the upper jaw the first is long and very narrow, pointing nearly horizontally forward. The next three teeth are enormous in size, very long, robust, pointed and slightly recurved.

facts.statement: According to many recent studies, Guidraco belongs to the subfamily Anhanguerinae within the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: According to many recent studies, Guidraco is a member of the group Anhanguerinae, a subfamily belonging to the larger group Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: In 2014, Brian Andres and colleagues recovered an alternate phylogenetic position for Guidraco within the family Boreopteridae.
facts.quote: Also in 2014, however, Brian Andres and colleagues recovered an alternate position for Guidraco among the family Boreopteridae, the cladogram of which is shown on the left.

facts.statement: Later analyses in 2019 reassigned Guidraco to the subfamily Anhanguerinae, identifying it as a sister taxon to the genera Caulkicephalus and Ludodactylus.
facts.quote: Later, in 2019, many subsequent analyses reassigned Guidraco to the family Anhangueridae, specifically to the subfamily Anhanguerinae, sister taxon to the genera Caulkicephalus and Ludodactylus.

facts.statement: Guidraco lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
